extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners (SPEs)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidelines for assigning/classifying U.S. (including PCT national phase) patent applications, transferring between art units and Technology Centers, and conducting prior-art searches and claim analysis during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment based on controlling claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be assigned like any other application, i.e., on the basis of the controlling claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governs assignment of U.S. national phase and PCT-associated national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of same-examiner assignment for PCT and U.S. national
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of having the U.S. national and PCT applications assigned to the same examiner is to promote consistent search and examination results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify assignment practices to improve consistency between international and national examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection of amendments that make transfer proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the receipt of an amendment which makes a transfer proper, steps should be taken promptly in accordance with the transfer procedure outlined in MPEP § 903.08(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt action required when amendments change proper classification or assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal transfer procedures within a Technology Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Technology Center (TC) has developed internal procedures for transferring applications between art units and resolving application assignment disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow TC-specific internal rules when transferring within the same TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPE-requested transfers between different Technology Centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an SPE believes an application (including PCT applications), either new or amended, does not belong in his or her art unit, he or she may request transfer of the application from his or her art unit to another art unit of a different TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PCT or docketed applications, assignment made by agreement between the SPEs involved. For undocketed non-PCT apps, agreement between SPEs or referral to the classification dispute TC representative panel if no agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full review before transfer to another TC
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an application is sent to a receiving art unit of a different TC, the application must be fully reviewed to ensure that all appropriate areas in the originating TC have been considered with respect to the classification of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When initiating transfer, the application must be sent on transfer inquiry to a receiving art unit; SPE must make best judgment even if application is confusing or contains unfamiliar subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer when application is 'best examinable' elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application’s claims include a combination of limitations for plural disciplines, an SPE or primary examiner may request transfer to another discipline on the ground that the application is 'best examinable' in the other discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requesting SPE/examiner should cite art showing the limitations classifiable in his/her discipline; see MPEP § 903.08(e) for examples and further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Transfer Request requirements (PALM EXPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: When transfer is appropriate, the SPE or primary examiner must complete the Application Transfer Request form in PALM EXPO and provide a full explanation of the reasons for classification in the receiving art unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An eDAN message should notify the receiving art unit. The form should include at least one of: (A) Identification of the controlling claim examinable in another TC; (B) Identification of any existing informal transfer agreement; (C) Other reasons with full explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult gatekeeper/search assistant when uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SPE or examiner of the originating art unit believes an application has been improperly assigned but is unable to determine an appropriate place to send it, a 'gatekeeper' or search assistant should be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing of gatekeepers/search assistants available; note that gatekeepers exist in all TCs except TC 2900 (design applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and refusal handling in transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving SPE or primary examiner agrees to accept the application, he or she classifies and assigns the application and effects the transfer by accepting the application in PALM EXPO. If the receiving SPE refuses, reasons must be entered in PALM EXPO and recorded; eDAN message should be sent for IFW applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If refused and app is undocketed non-PCT, originating art unit may accept for examination or forward to classification dispute panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification dispute TC representative panel authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If SPEs cannot agree on classification, the application may be forwarded to the classification dispute TC representative panel of the TC where the application was originally assigned for a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel consists of designated representatives from each TC and may, in certain circumstances, assign an application to a class or art unit contrary to controlling classification rules if better equipped to examine the application (see MPEP § 903.08(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate a better class when contesting assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: In contesting the assignment of an application, the SPE or primary examiner should indicate another class that is a better class in which to classify the application, rather than simply arguing that the application does not fit the examiner’s class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggested alternative classification with supporting rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve non-classification issues before transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains both classification issues and issues unrelated to classification (e.g., a dispute as to the propriety of restriction), the issues unrelated to classification should be resolved first. If classification issues remain, transfer may be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 903.08(e) for procedure where examining corps issues are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of special applications during transfer (PCT and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty and such other special applications must be hand-carried throughout the transfer process unless an established practice is in place for expediting delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hand-carried at any stage, update application location on PALM system each time the application is moved.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIPE class/subclass mismatch handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application has been assigned a class/subclass by the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE) and routed to an art unit that does not examine applications assigned that class/subclass, an 'OIPEClass/GAUMismatch' IFW mailbox eDAN message should be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures routing mismatches are flagged and corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of nonprovisional applications follows classification principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment of nonprovisional applications follows, as far as possible, the rules or principles governing the classification of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications generally assigned where the application would have an original classification if the claims were in a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for original classification referenced to MPEP §903.07
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria by which the original classification is determined are set forth in MPEP § 903.07.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP § 903.07 for detailed classification criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read claims in light of the disclosure; do not go behind the record
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims and statement of invention are generally taken as they read; however, claims must be read in light of the disclosure (claimed disclosure). Any attempt to go behind the record and decide the case upon what is deemed the 'real invention' would introduce more errors than it would cure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs cannot possess specific knowledge of all art; such merit questions are for the examiners to determine and may be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose most indented subclass within a class
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a class, looking down from the top of the schedule, the OR subclass is chosen from among the classifications of the claimed disclosure according to whichever one is the most indented subclass of the first subclass array.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow hierarchical indentation when selecting subclass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior patents' location generally controls assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The location of the United States patents constituting the prior art is generally controlling over all else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where time permits, obvious misplacements of patents constituting the prior art are corrected, but wholesale reclassification is impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assign based on only a single element of a combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, an application cannot be assigned to a class which includes one element or part only of several claimed in combination. The claim is treated in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment must consider full combination recited in claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer on 'best examinable' basis may require citation of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where assignment for examination is on a 'best examinable' basis, the person requesting the transfer is ordinarily required to cite references pertinent to the claimed features falling under the jurisdiction of the art within his or her discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application of the reference(s) is not evident, the transferring examiner should include a brief statement explaining the relation and possible application; the classification dispute panel can require such a statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements should be made without seeking transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application has been taken up by an examiner for action and a requirement to restrict is found necessary, an action requiring restriction should be made without seeking a transfer of the case to another TC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's reply to the restriction requirement may make a transfer unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of composition/alloy-only claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, where all the claims of an application are for an article made of a specific composition or alloy with no other structure of the article recited, the application will be assigned to the composition or alloy class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat composition-only claims as composition-class cases for assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place cases with no clear rule where best searched and adjudicated
rubrics_metrics.description: A class of cases exists in which either no art or a divided art is found and in which no rule or principle is involved; such cases are placed where they will be best searched and adjudicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often no clear reason can be given for such placements; balance of considerations may guide decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searcher/examiner should search both own and target class when seeking transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner seeking the transfer of a case may make a search of both his or her own class and the class to which he or she thinks the case should be transferred, and the examiner in charge should ensure the record includes the result of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of searches should be in the record to support transfer requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification dispute panel returns non-classification issues to originating TC
rubrics_metrics.description: When the classification dispute panel receives an application with matters under dispute not related to classification (e.g., propriety of a restriction requirement, timeliness of submission), the application will be returned to the originating TC for resolution on the issues unrelated to classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen newly received applications immediately so unrelated issues are promptly returned to originating TC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions of classification dispute panel are final and binding
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification dispute TC representative panel will evaluate evidence presented and make a decision on the proper classification and assignment of the application; the decision of the panel will be final and binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel conferences between TC representatives may be set up to resolve disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PALM EXPO EXPO Transfer Inquiry function
rubrics_metrics.description: SPEs and examiners must use the EXPO Transfer Inquiry function, which creates a record of the transfer inquiry history of each application and facilitates tracking of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PALM EXPO provides a routing sheet to be included in the application file when a transfer inquiry is created.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Int. Cl. symbols on issuing documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Strasbourg Agreement, the United States is required to indicate on its issuing documents the International Patent Classification 2006 (Eighth Edition) (Int. Cl.) classification symbols of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Int. Cl. symbols must be placed in the indicated space on the Image File Wrapper (IFW) issue classification form when an application is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Int. Cl. layout (sections/classes/subclasses/groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Int. Cl. layout comprises Section (A–H), Class (section + two-digit number), Subclass (class + capital letter), and Group (subclass + numbers separated by '/'), forming the complete classification symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on reading subgroup digits as decimal subdivisions, and on guide headings, main group and subgroup titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Int. Cl. subclass effective scope using title, references, and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective scope of a subclass is defined by (A) the subclass title, (B) any references following the subclass or higher class title, (C) references in groups or guide headings, and (D) any notes or definitions appearing under the subclass title or its class/subsection/section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and notes can substantially alter the apparent scope of a subclass; consult volume 9 of Int. Cl. Classification for more procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret main groups and subgroups within effective scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a main group or subgroup is to be interpreted only within the effective scope of its subclass or main group, determined by titles as modified by relevant references or notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guide headings are informative and normally do not modify scope except where clear from context; subgroup titles are dependent on the titles above them.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S.–Int. Cl. Concordance is a guide, not a literal translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Concordance between U.S. classes/subclasses and the Int. Cl. is a guide to be used in conjunction with the Int. Cl., and not as a translation list; complete one-to-one correspondence cannot be attained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concordance is updated monthly and may contain errors; examiners should suggest corrections to the TC classification contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain a thorough understanding before searching
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner, after having obtained a thorough understanding of the invention disclosed and claimed, then searches the prior art as disclosed in patents and other published documents (nonpatent literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inventor name searches to identify other applications/patents relevant to double patenting; review parent applications in continuing applications; consider international search reports for national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of first search—should avoid need for second search
rubrics_metrics.description: The first search should be such that the examiner need not ordinarily make a second search of the prior art, unless necessitated by amendments to the claims in the first reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First search should cover the invention as described and claimed, including inventive concepts toward which the claims appear directed; should not be extended merely to add immaterial variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record search details on IFW search notes form (first action)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits, the examiner must complete the IFW search notes form in OACS to include the classes and subclasses of domestic and foreign patents, abstract collections, and publications in which the search was made, other information collections/sources, and the date(s) of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In subsequent actions, indicate that the search has been updated and identify the additional field(s) of search; any search updates should include relevant databases and the search queries and classifications employed in the original search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully analyze claim breadth; apply broadest reasonable interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The breadth of the claims in the application should always be carefully noted; the examiner should be fully aware of what the claims do not call for as well as what they do require. During patent examination, the claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2111–§ 2116.01 and In re Morris for case law on claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize variant embodiments within claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantially every claim includes within its breadth one or more variant embodiments not disclosed in the application but which would anticipate the claimed invention if found in a reference; the claim must be so analyzed and any such variant encountered during the search should be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For apparatus/machine claims, sketching or diagramming the subject matter as defined by the claim (including multiple divergent sketches) assists in determining the claim's actual breadth. Applicants are not required to submit such sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider equivalents unless expressly excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: All subject matter that is the equivalent of the subject matter as defined in the claim, even though specifically different from the definition in the claim, must be considered unless expressly excluded by the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2181–§ 2184 for discussion of equivalents when claim employs means- or step-plus-function terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider analogous arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of analogous arts is required when determining what references are pertinent to a claim (904.01(c) heading indicates analogous arts discussion follows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply the principle of analogous arts when searching for relevant prior art (full guidance in subsequent text).
